title: Variational Autoencoders (VAE) on Fashion-MNIST: Latent Sampling & Loss Functions

assessment_targets.what_taught_summary: The VAE encoder is a Keras Sequential model with Dense layers (256, 128 units, ReLU) that outputs two distinct tensors: z_mean and z_log_var, representing the parameters of the latent distribution.
assessment_targets.why_assessed_pedagogy: To ensure students can identify the specific architectural components and output structure required to define a probabilistic latent space, distinguishing it from a standard autoencoder.
misconception_distractor_hints: The encoder outputs a single deterministic vector z directly without separate mean and variance tensors.
The final layer of the encoder uses a Sigmoid activation to constrain the latent vector to [0, 1].
The encoder uses Conv2D layers exclusively to process the 28x28 image input before flattening.

assessment_targets.what_taught_summary: Latent sampling utilizes the reparameterization trick where z is calculated as z = μ + exp(0.5 * log_var) * ε, with ε sampled from a standard normal distribution N(0, 1).
assessment_targets.why_assessed_pedagogy: To verify that students recall the specific mathematical mechanism used to make the sampling process differentiable during backpropagation.
misconception_distractor_hints: The noise term ε is sampled from a uniform distribution U(0, 1).
The variance term is used directly as σ in the formula z = μ + σ * ε without the exponential transformation.
The sampling layer is a standard Dense layer that performs a linear combination of inputs.

assessment_targets.what_taught_summary: The total VAE loss function is the sum of the reconstruction loss (e.g., binary cross-entropy) and the KL divergence term, which regularizes the latent space to match a standard normal prior.
assessment_targets.why_assessed_pedagogy: To confirm students can identify the two fundamental components of the VAE objective function and their respective roles in balancing reconstruction accuracy and latent space regularization.
misconception_distractor_hints: The KL divergence term measures the difference between the input image and the reconstructed image.
The reconstruction loss is calculated using Mean Squared Error (MSE) exclusively, regardless of data type.
The total loss is the product of the reconstruction loss and the KL divergence term.

assessment_targets.what_taught_summary: Fashion-MNIST data is preprocessed by normalizing pixel values to the [0, 1] range (dividing by 255.0) and expanding dimensions to (28, 28, 1) for model input compatibility.
assessment_targets.why_assessed_pedagogy: To ensure students remember the specific data preprocessing steps required to adapt the Fashion-MNIST dataset for use with the VAE architecture.
misconception_distractor_hints: Pixel values are normalized to the [-1, 1] range by subtracting 127.5 and dividing by 127.5.
The input shape remains (28, 28) without expanding the channel dimension.
The dataset is one-hot encoded before being fed into the encoder.

assessment_targets.what_taught_summary: The model training setup involves a Keras Sequential encoder with Dense layers (256, 128 units, ReLU) outputting z_mean and z_log_var, which are then used in the reparameterization formula for training.
assessment_targets.why_assessed_pedagogy: To verify that students can recall the specific model configuration and the integration of the encoder outputs into the training pipeline.
misconception_distractor_hints: The encoder uses Dropout layers after every Dense layer to prevent overfitting.
The z_mean and z_log_var tensors are concatenated before being passed to the decoder.
The model is trained using a standard Autoencoder loss function without the KL divergence term.
